newsitem.title: UK: KS Biomedix to make anti muscle-ageing drug.
newsitem.headline: KS Biomedix to make anti muscle-ageing drug.

text.p: A drug is being developed which could reverse the ageing process of muscles and speed recovery from sports injuries, fledgling biotech company KS Biomedix Holdings Plc said on Thursday.

The Guildford-based group, which was floated on the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) in October 1995, said in a statement it had acquired intellectual property rights to research into treatment of ageing muscles carried out the Charing Cross and Westminster Medical School in London.

In a telephone interview with Reuters managing director Kim Tan said "this is a big market area, with a growing ageing population around the world. We all care about being able to stay fit for a lot longer and be active for a lot longer."

Tan said scientists had identified key chemical changes which occur when muscles deteriorate, and developed an entity which can enhance the muscle's elasticity. The company's aim is to develop an oral drug or a patch to take advantage of the discovery.
As well as being suited to older people and those who are bedridden, Tan said the drug could be useful for speeding up recovery from damage caused by sports injuries and surgery.

The entity developed by researchers at Charing Cross grew out of work by the Royal College of Surgeons to drastically cut the death rate in open heart surgery. The team built up a useful knowledge about the elasticity of heart muscles.

KS Biomedix, which is also developing drugs to treat rheumatoid arthritis and diabetes, said it would take the drug through Phase I and Phase II clinical trials before seeking partners to share the costs of the work.
Tam said there is no timetable for the start of clinical trials.
